name: Industry Surveys of AI Adoption
blurb: What surveys say about AI use in healthcare and life sciences.
title: Industry Surveys of AI Adoption
answer: Vendor and industry surveys show AI use is now the norm in life sciences. NVIDIA's 2025 survey of healthcare and life sciences organisations found most actively using AI and a large majority expecting it to transform the industry within three to five years, and Salesforce's 2025 survey found nearly all life sciences leaders expect AI agents to become essential.

crumbs.name: AI Adoption and Governance in Life Sciences

reading.body:
Vendor surveys show near-universal expectation of AI transformation in life sciences, but they measure sentiment, not results.

The pattern across the two 2025 surveys is expectation rather than evidence. NVIDIA found 83 percent of healthcare and life sciences respondents agreeing AI will revolutionise the field within three to five years. Salesforce found nearly all life sciences leaders expecting AI agents to become essential within two years. Both figures describe what people believe will happen, not what has been measured to happen.

That distinction matters for AI specifically because the binding constraints on deployment are physical. Compute has to be bought, buildings have to be powered and cooled, and regulated life sciences work has to clear validation before any of it reaches production. A survey can register enthusiasm for agents without registering whether the power and compute behind them exist. The data here does not connect adoption claims to any infrastructure measure, so it cannot tell you whether the expected transformation is funded or merely anticipated.

The surveys also come from vendors with an interest in the answer, and the data itself flags selection and framing bias as a known limitation. What it does not cover is outcomes: time saved, quality, cost per task, or whether any organisation that reported using AI kept using it. Read the numbers as direction of travel, and measure your own programme on what it actually produces.

terms.line: The field of computer science dedicated to creating systems that perform tasks typically requiring human intelligence: understanding language, recognizing patterns, making decisions.

Models that create new content, text, images, video, audio, code, from patterns learned in training data. The 2022 shift from AI that classifies to AI that produces is what put this glossary on your reading list.

siblings.name: Governing AI in a Regulated Company

explainer:
Surveys from technology vendors, consultancies and industry groups regularly report high and rising AI adoption in health care and life sciences, along with strong expectations for agents and generative AI. They are useful for spotting trends and common priorities.

They also have limits. Many are run by companies that sell AI, samples are often self selected, questions measure intentions and perceptions rather than results, and definitions of use vary. Treat survey figures as indicators of sentiment and direction, and judge your own programme on measured outcomes.
